question: A force-combination model uses the vectors $\vec{F}\_1=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{F}\_2=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}$. A third force is defined as $\vec{F}\_3=2\vec{F}\_2$. After finding the combined force, students must determine an equilibrant $\vec{E}$ having the same magnitude as the resultant but acting in its opposite direction. The model allows them to examine vector addition, scalar multiplication and the negative of a vector.(a) Calculate $\vec{F}\_1+\vec{F}\_2$.(b) Determine $\vec{F}\_3$.(c) Find the resultant $\vec{F}=\vec{F}\_1+\vec{F}\_2+\vec{F}\_3$.(d) Obtain the equilibrant $\vec{E}$ and justify its relationship with $\vec{F}$.
explanation: (a)`\vec{F}_1+\vec{F}_2=(2-1)\hat{i}+(-1+2)\hat{j}+(3+1)\hat{k}\vec{F}_1+\vec{F}_2=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+4\hat{k}`(b)`\vec{F}_3=2\vec{F}_2\vec{F}_3=2(-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})\vec{F}_3=-2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+2\hat{k}`(c)`\vec{F}=(\vec{F}_1+\vec{F}_2)+\vec{F}_3\vec{F}=(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+4\hat{k})+(-2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\vec{F}=-\hat{i}+5\hat{j}+6\hat{k}`(d)The equilibrant is the negative of the resultant. Therefore,`\vec{E}=-\vec{F}\vec{E}=\hat{i}-5\hat{j}-6\hat{k}`The corresponding components of $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{F}$ differ only in sign. Hence, they have equal magnitudes and opposite directions.
